title: Franconia Ridge via Falling Waters
blurb: Waterfalls on the way up, then the classic knife-edge ridge above treeline. Pair with Old Bridle Path for the 8.9-mile loop. Very busy on fall weekends; the lot fills before 7 am.

title: Artist's Bluff
blurb: A short, steep scramble to the most photographed view in Franconia Notch: Echo Lake and Cannon Mountain in full color.

title: Mount Willard
blurb: An old carriage road to a ledge with the whole of Crawford Notch laid out below. Big payoff for moderate effort.

title: Chocorua via Champney Falls
blurb: Off the Kancamagus, past Champney and Pitcher Falls to Chocorua's bare rocky summit.

title: Mount Monadnock (White Dot)
blurb: One of the most-climbed mountains in the world. A steep, rocky route to a bare summit with views across three states.

title: Arethusa Falls
blurb: New Hampshire's tallest waterfall through hardwood forest in Crawford Notch.

title: Mount Major
blurb: Lake Winnipesaukee from an open summit. Short and popular, so go early or on a weekday.

title: Mount Cardigan (West Ridge)
blurb: Open granite summit with a fire tower and 360° views over a sea of hardwoods.

title: West Rattlesnake
blurb: A gentle climb to ledges over Squam Lake, the On Golden Pond view.

title: Pawtuckaway fire tower
blurb: A short climb to a fire tower in Pawtuckaway State Park, with boulder fields nearby.

title: Lincoln Woods
blurb: A flat old railroad grade along the Pemigewasset River, starting from the Kancamagus Highway.
grandma: Wide and nearly flat. Cross the suspension bridge from the lot and walk as far as you like along the river.

title: The Flume Gorge
blurb: Boardwalks through a granite gorge in Franconia Notch. Timed tickets from the state park.
grandma: Boardwalks and stairs in the gorge; a shuttle bus covers part of the way.

title: Mount Mansfield (Sunset Ridge)
blurb: An open ridge most of the way to the Chin, Vermont's highest point, with Lake Champlain behind you.

title: Stowe Pinnacle
blurb: A short, steep climb to a rocky knob looking straight across Stowe's valley at Mount Mansfield.

title: Camel's Hump (Burrows)
blurb: The most direct route up Vermont's most recognizable summit.

title: Mount Tom, Woodstock
blurb: Gentle switchbacks to the South Peak over Woodstock village and its church steeples.

title: Quechee Gorge
blurb: Vermont's deepest gorge, seen from the Route 4 bridge and a riverside trail.
grandma: The bridge overlook is right by the visitor center lot; the trail down to the river is a steeper option.

title: Owl's Head, Groton
blurb: Open ledges over Kettle Pond and Lake Groton in Groton State Forest.

title: Elmore Mountain
blurb: A fire tower over Lake Elmore and the Worcester Range.

title: Gile Mountain
blurb: A short climb to a fire tower above the Connecticut River valley near Norwich.

title: The Beehive, Acadia
blurb: Iron rungs up a cliff face above Sand Beach. Not for anyone afraid of heights.

title: Ocean Path, Acadia
blurb: Along the granite shore from Sand Beach to Otter Point, past Thunder Hole.
grandma: Mostly level gravel with a few steps. Lots of parking pull-offs along Park Loop Road, so you can walk a short piece.

title: Jordan Pond
blurb: A loop around a clear pond under the Bubbles. Popovers at Jordan Pond House afterward.
grandma: The east shore is smooth gravel; the west side has rocks and boardwalk. Walk out and back along the east shore.

title: Gorham Mountain, Acadia
blurb: Open ledges with ocean views, an easier alternative to the Beehive.

title: Cadillac Mountain summit
blurb: A paved loop around the top of Acadia's highest peak. Vehicle reservations needed in season.
grandma: Paved and nearly flat, right next to the summit parking.

title: Tumbledown Mountain
blurb: A rugged climb to an alpine pond tucked between summits in Maine's western mountains.

title: Table Rock, Grafton Notch
blurb: A slab of rock jutting out over Grafton Notch, with Old Speck across the way.

title: Mount Battie, Camden
blurb: A short steep climb to a stone tower over Camden Harbor and Penobscot Bay. You can also drive up.

title: Maiden Cliff
blurb: Cliffs over Megunticook Lake, one of the best foliage views in midcoast Maine.

title: Bald Rock Mountain
blurb: A quieter Camden Hills summit looking out over the islands of Penobscot Bay.

title: Mount Greylock (Cheshire Harbor)
blurb: A steady climb to the highest point in Massachusetts. You can also drive to the top.

title: Monument Mountain
blurb: Where Melville and Hawthorne met in 1850. Quartzite cliffs over the Housatonic Valley.

title: Bash Bish Falls
blurb: The state's highest single-drop waterfall, in a steep gorge at the corner of three states.

title: Mount Wachusett (Pine Hill)
blurb: The shortest, steepest way up Wachusett. On a clear day you can see Boston and Monadnock.

title: Mount Sugarloaf
blurb: A summit tower over the Connecticut River's oxbow and farm fields.
grandma: The summit road usually leads right to the observation tower; the trail is the steeper way.

title: Blue Hills Skyline
blurb: Rocky ups and downs over the Blue Hills with the Boston skyline in view. Great close to the city.

title: Mount Holyoke
blurb: To the Summit House on the Holyoke Range, high over the Connecticut River.

title: Fresh Pond, Cambridge
blurb: A loop around the reservoir with maples, oaks and benches all the way.
grandma: Paved, level and lined with benches.

title: Norwottuck Rail Trail
blurb: A paved rail trail between Northampton and Belchertown, crossing the Connecticut River.
grandma: Paved and flat. Start at Elwell State Park for the river bridge, and walk as far as you like.

title: Haystack Mountain
blurb: A stone tower in Norfolk with views into three states.

title: Breakheart Pond, Arcadia
blurb: Around a quiet pond in Rhode Island's largest forest. One of the last places in New England to peak.

title: Blackstone River Bikeway
blurb: A paved path between the Blackstone River and the old canal, past mill villages.
grandma: Paved and level with benches. Many access points with parking.

title: Monadnock Cliff Walk
blurb: A ledgy route along Monadnock's flank to Thoreau's Seat and Bald Rock, quieter than the summit.
